q: 1. Construction site planning mainly depends upon the
explain: Effective site planning must account for ground and space conditions, the specific engineering nature of the project, and the required construction methodologies.

q: 2. The upper portion of horizontal bars in a bar chart indicates
options: total duration for completion of an activity
progress of work in the specified time
due duration for the completion of an activity
explain: In specialized bar charts, the upper portion of the bar is often used to shade or hatch the actual progress made relative to the total scheduled duration.

q: 3. In the network shown in Fig., the concurrent and preceding activities corresponding to activity 2-4 are respectively
explain: From the given network diagram, activity 2-3 runs concurrently with 2-4 (both starting from node 2), while 1-2 precedes it - matching answer key option b.

q: 4. The maximum number of head event occurring in a CPM is
explain: Similarly, a project network should converge to exactly one single end event (head event).

q: 5. Whenever activity has zero total float, then
options: free float of the activity must be zero but independent float need not be zero
independent float must be zero but free float need not be zero
free float and independent float both must be zero
free float and independent float both need not be zero
explain: Since total float is the 'parent' float, if it is zero, all other sub-types of float (free and independent) must also be zero.

q: 6. Work study comprises
explain: Work study = method study + work measurement.

q: 7. Actual performance of a task is called
explain: An activity represents the actual performance of work/task in a project.

q: 8. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Positive float indicates the activity has spare time available and can be delayed without affecting the project, making it sub-critical.

q: 9. Latest start time is the
options: latest time by which an activity can be started without delaying the project
latest time by which an activity can be completed without delaying the project
latest time the event can occur
explain: Latest Start Time (LST) is the maximum delay possible for the start of a task that won't push back the project completion date.

q: 10. Resource smoothening means
options: adjustment of resources to have the least variations
complete renovation if resources suit the requirement
optimization and economical utilization of resources
explain: Resource smoothening rearranges non-critical activities within their float to minimize fluctuations in resource demand while keeping project duration fixed.

q: 11. The latest allowable time for any event i is equal to
explain: During backward pass calculations, the Latest Allowable Occurring Time T_L for an event is computed as the minimum of (T_L^j - t^ij).

q: 12. Float may be defined as the difference between
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and the time required to complete the activity
explain: All three expressions give the float.

q: 13. The figure [bursting arrows] indicates
explain: When multiple activity arrows originate from a single event node, it is known as a burst event.

q: 14. Critical path
explain: The critical path is the longest path through the network; therefore, it contains the activities with the least amount of flexibility or 'minimum slack' (usually zero).

q: 15. The area under the β-distribution curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time divides the area into two equal halves, so there is a 50% chance on either side.

q: 16. The artificial activity which indicates that an activity following it, cannot be started unless the preceding activity is complete, is known as
explain: A dummy activity is an artificial, zero-duration link used to enforce correct dependency/precedence relationships in the network.

q: 17. The amount of time required performing any event in case of PERT should be ................... CPM.
explain: Because PERT deals with uncertain/probabilistic time estimates and CPM uses deterministic ones, the actual time required can vary based on the nature of the project.

q: 18. The difference between the time available to do a job and the time required to do the job, is known as
explain: Float (slack) is defined as the difference between available time and required time for completing an activity.

q: 19. Critical path lies along the activities having total float
explain: Activities on the critical path always have zero total float by definition.

q: 20. Select the incorrect statement
options: start float and finish float are always equal
total float can be either start float or finish float
start float and finish float need not be equal
start float and finish float are the differences between activity times and not event times
explain: Per the answer key, c. Note: standard theory says start and finish float are equal for an activity, so the key looks questionable.

q: 21. The benefit of the PERT network is taken by the management in
options: readjusting the time to meet the target
explain: PERT provides a comprehensive framework for scheduling, inter-departmental coordination, and dynamic readjustment based on probability.

q: 22. PERT analysis is based on
explain: PERT analysis relies on all three time estimates to calculate the expected mean time.

q: 23. In PERT analysis the actual performance of task is known as
explain: The actual work or performance required to progress from one event to another is termed an activity.

q: 24. In a barchart the vertical axis represents
explain: Activities are listed on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis.

q: 25. The activity which is crashed first has
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: Crashing follows a least-cost approach, starting with the critical activity having the least (lowest) cost slope to minimize the additional cost incurred.

q: 26. The probability distribution taken to represent the completion time in PERT analysis is
explain: PERT assumes activity times follow the beta distribution.

q: 27. The optimistic, most likely and pessimistic time estimates of an activity are 5, 10, 21 days, what are the expected time and standard deviation?
28. Crash project duration is obtained by adding the
options: crash durations for all the activities
normal duration for all the activities
normal duration for all the activities along the critical path
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path
explain: The total crashed duration is the sum of the crash times of all activities forming the critical path.

q: 29. A frequency distribution curve
options: having single lump is called unimodal curve
if symmetrical is called normal curve
if unsymmetrical is called skew curve
explain: These are standard statistical terms describing the shape and symmetry of frequency distributions.

q: 30. The pictorial representation of activity and event of a project is known as
explain: The pictorial diagram showing activities and events with their interrelationships in a project is called a network diagram.

q: 31. Technical planning is carried out for the
options: planning resource and initiating procurement action
explain: Technical planning encompasses preparing detailed drawings, estimates, and resource/procurement planning - all these activities together.

q: 32. An activity is
explain: An activity in a project network is a specific portion of work that consumes time and resources to complete.

q: 33. Technical planning is carried out for the
explain: Technical planning covers drawings and the detailed estimate.

q: 34. Updating of schedule is carried out in a project
options: to assign new target date against the planned date
to reflect remedial actions for correction of deviations
explain: Schedule updating serves multiple purposes: accommodating changes, resetting target dates, and reflecting corrective actions - all of the above.

its earliest finish time and latest time for its successor activity

q: 37. Aggregate planning is planning for
explain: Aggregate planning looks at the total capacity and resource needs for the entire project rather than individual small tasks.

q: 38. Which one is the basis of project?
explain: A project is built on the pillars of planning what to do, scheduling when to do it, and monitoring to ensure it is done correctly.

options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event tie of preceding node

options: top right, outside the circle, in triangle
top right, outside the circle, in rectangle
explain: Per the answer key, in a rectangle at the top right, outside the circle.

q: 41. CPM stand for:
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method.

q: 42. A CPM network is updated
options: whenever there is differences in the planned and actual performance
explain: Network updating is done whenever a deviation is found between planned and actual performance, requiring revision.

q: 43. Bar chart is also known as
explain: A bar chart is also called a Gantt chart.

q: 44. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is called
explain: The network diagram is the standard pictorial representation depicting a project's activities and events with their interrelationships.

q: 45. The object of technical planning, is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
explain: Technical planning covers preparing specifications, estimates, and initiating resource procurement - all of the above.
